recommendations.title: Make readiness reflect subsystem health, and alert on /status/health
recommendations.rationale: In experiment f63b02a3c8ac (risk HIGH 6.2/10), API success fell to 0% during injection, TTR 26 s, findings: API success dropped to 0% during the fault; things-search kept reporting /ready=200 while the API was failing. The service kept answering `/ready` with 200 while the API was failing, so no orchestrator or alert could react. Ditto issue #1865 describes exactly this: the Pekko cluster was healthy but the persistence subsystem was not, and PR #1867 added a `subsystem-health` check under `management.health-checks.liveness-checks`.
steps: Upgrade to a Ditto release containing PR #1867 (3.6+) and confirm `management.health-checks.liveness-checks.subsystem-health` is enabled.

Verify whether the equivalent subsystem check is wired into the readiness checks for your version; if not, add it (or treat `/status/health` as the readiness probe in compose/k8s instead of `/ready`).
Point the compose `healthcheck` of each Ditto service at `http://localhost:8558/status/health` (requires devops credentials or `DEVOPS_SECURED=false` in the lab) and fail on any `DOWN` component.
Add a Prometheus alert on `probe_success{job="ditto-health"} == 0` and on the API error-rate SLO, not only on `/alive`.
verify: Stop mongodb: within one healthcheck interval the Ditto services report `unhealthy` in `docker ps` and `/status/health` shows the persistence component `DOWN`.
The `health_check_masked_failure` finding no longer appears when the experiment is replayed.

recommendations.title: Automate recovery after dependency outages: reconnect/backoff, health-keyed restarts, alert rule
recommendations.rationale: In experiment f63b02a3c8ac (risk HIGH 6.2/10), API success fell to 0% during injection, TTR 26 s, findings: API success dropped to 0% during the fault; things-search kept reporting /ready=200 while the API was failing. The service did not come back on its own once its dependency returned; the injector had to restart it. Ditto discussion #1861 reports the same symptom (Things did not reconnect to MongoDB after an outage). In production this is a page at 03:00 for something a restart policy could do.
steps: Review the Pekko persistence / Mongo driver reconnect settings for the affected service (restart-on-failure backoff in `ditto-*.conf`); make sure the persistence actors are restarted with exponential backoff rather than stopped after N failures.

Add a Docker healthcheck that hits `/status/health` and an `autoheal` sidecar (or Kubernetes liveness probe) so an `unhealthy` service is restarted automatically — `restart: always` ignores health state.
Add a Prometheus alert: `probe_success{instance=~"things|policies|gateway"} == 0 for 1m` and `rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[2m]) / rate(http_requests_total[2m]) > 0.05 for 2m`.
Document a runbook entry: 'if X is unhealthy after Mongo returns, `docker compose restart X`' until the automated path is proven.
verify: Replay the experiment; `recovery.remediation_actions` in the report must be empty and `recovered=true`.
The alert fires in Prometheus/Alertmanager during the outage window.

recommendations.title: Scale things horizontally and make clients retry with idempotent, ETag-guarded writes
recommendations.rationale: In experiment f63b02a3c8ac (risk HIGH 6.2/10), API success fell to 0% during injection, TTR 26 s, findings: API success dropped to 0% during the fault; things-search kept reporting /ready=200 while the API was failing. Things actors are cluster-sharded, so a second instance lets Pekko re-home shards instead of waiting for the crashed JVM to restart. On the client side, every Thing write in Ditto is a PUT with `If-Match`/ETag support, so retries are safe and cheap.
steps: Run `things` with `deploy.replicas: 2` (compose) or `replicas: 2` (k8s); keep the Pekko seed-node list stable.
Set a sensible `pekko.cluster.sharding.rebalance-interval` / `passivation` so shards move within a few seconds of a node loss.
In client SDKs, wrap PUT/PATCH with 3 retries + exponential backoff on 5xx/connection errors and send `If-Match: <etag>` to make the retry idempotent; treat 412 as 'already applied'.
Keep POST-created things (server-generated ids) behind a client-side idempotency key or prefer PUT with a client-chosen thingId.
verify: Kill one things instance: API success stays > 90% and the cluster view shows the shard regions rebalanced.
A retried PUT with a stale `If-Match` returns 412 rather than overwriting newer state.

recommendations.title: Baseline observability: SLO alert rules and chaos annotations in Grafana
recommendations.rationale: In experiment f63b02a3c8ac (risk HIGH 6.2/10), API success fell to 0% during injection, TTR 26 s, findings: API success dropped to 0% during the fault; things-search kept reporting /ready=200 while the API was failing. Whatever the specific fault, the first production improvement is knowing within a minute that users are affected. Alert on what the user sees (probe success, error rate, p95), not only on container liveness.
steps: Prometheus rules: `probe_success == 0 for 1m` (blackbox on `/api/2/things` through nginx), API error-rate SLO burn (`sum(rate(requests{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests[5m])) > 0.02`), and `histogram_quantile(0.95, ...) > 1s for 5m`.
Add a Grafana annotation (HTTP API `POST /api/annotations`, tag `chaos`) at the start and end of each Faultline experiment so latency spikes are attributable.
Dashboard the Docker health state per container (`container_health_status` via cAdvisor or a tiny exporter) next to the API SLIs.
verify: During the next experiment an alert fires within 60 s of the first API error and the Grafana graph shows the chaos window.
